items.title: Sudan: Commercial Diplomacy Starts With Connections
items.description: [U.S. Embassy Khartoum] Chargé d'Affaires Jonathan Howard and the Office of Sudan Affairs hosted a reception in Cairo bringing together approximately 60 Sudanese business leaders, Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI) alumni, and representatives from U.S. Embassy Cairo's Foreign Commercial Service. The gathering focused on strengthening U.S.-Sudanese commercial ties and building networks that can support Sudan's eventual post-war economic recovery.

items.title: Egypt to build a rail link as an alternative to the blocked Suez Canal
items.description: Dubbed the "Suez Canal on Rails", the line connects Red Sea ports directly to Mediterranean export terminals. Once fully operational, it is expected to carry up to 13 million tonnes of freight each year, allowing cargo to be transferred across Egypt by rail and helping bypass maritime bottlenecks.
items.titleIt: Egypt to build a rail link as an alternative to the blocked Suez Canal

items.title: Somalia braces for El Niño floods as millions face risk of hunger
items.description: In Bayahaaw village, on the outskirts of Jowhar in central Somalia, farmers face a difficult choice: plant crops and risk losing them to floodwaters or leave their fields bare and face potential hunger in the coming year. Nuh Adan, a farmer and community leader in Bayahaaw, said flooding caused by breached riverbanks could devastate local agriculture for months. "If the river breaks and the floods hit us, the effects will last until the next rainy season in March," Adan said. items.titleIt: Somalia braces for El Niño floods as millions face risk of hunger

items.title: Somalia: Xawaadle Elders and Al-Shabaab Reportedly Reach Truce in Hiiraan
items.description: A 16-point joint statement circulated by Al-Shabaab-affiliated media  said the sides had resolved their disputes and agreed to maintain peace in areas controlled or influenced by the clan. The reported agreement includes a commitment by Hawadle elders not to allow the recruitment or operation of Macawiisley fighters in their areas or provide them with shelter. Macawiisley forces from Hiiraan have played a key role in supporting Somali government troops against Al-Shabaab. The meeting in Maxaas was attended by dozens of traditional elders, while Al-Shabaab was represented by senior figures

items.description: A health facility has also been damaged, according to the UN Children's Fund, UNICEF, and other humanitarian agencies. items.description: Residents reported hearing a series of powerful explosions across Baidoa, with thick plumes of smoke visible over parts of the city. items.description: The boat went down during the night of Oct. 8-9 near Guehere, north of the port town of Obock. items.titleIt: Death toll rises to 139 after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti

items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 14 OTT - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday thanked Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni for her support and unequivocal stance in condemning a diesel deal between United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin as risky and a legitimisation of Moscow. items.title: Somalia: Heavy Fighting Erupts in Baidoa as Rival Forces Trade Claims
items.description: Residents reported hearing a series of powerful explosions across Baidoa, with thick plumes of smoke visible over parts of the city. Initial reports indicated that several locations, including a power facility and a base used by federal government forces, were struck during the clashes. items.title: Sudan: Commercial Diplomacy Starts With Connections
items.description: [U.S. Embassy Khartoum] Chargé d'Affaires Jonathan Howard and the Office of Sudan Affairs hosted a reception in Cairo bringing together approximately 60 Sudanese business leaders, Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI) alumni, and representatives from U.S. Embassy Cairo's Foreign Commercial Service. The gathering focused on strengthening U.S.-Sudanese commercial ties and building networks that can support Sudan's eventual post-war economic recovery.

items.title: Egypt to build a rail link as an alternative to the blocked Suez Canal
items.description: Dubbed the "Suez Canal on Rails", the line connects Red Sea ports directly to Mediterranean export terminals. Once fully operational, it is expected to carry up to 13 million tonnes of freight each year, allowing cargo to be transferred across Egypt by rail and helping bypass maritime bottlenecks.
